'''''Chaetomorpha linum''''' is a species of [[green algae]] in the family ''[[Cladophoraceae]]''.

''Chaetomorpha linum'' and ''[[Chaetomorpha aerea]]'' are considered by some authors to be conspecific.<ref name="Burrows">Burrows, E.M. 1991. ''Seaweeds of the British Isles Volume 2 Chlorophyta.'' Natural History Museum, London</ref> This is not accepted by other authorities.<ref>Hardy, F.G. and Guiry, M.D. 2003. ''A Check-list and Atlas of the Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.'' The British Phycological Society {{ISBN|0-9527115-16}}.</ref>

==Description==
''Chaetomorpha linum'' is a species composed of fine hair-like, uniseriate, unbranched filaments. Cells 1 - 2 times as long as broad, maximum width 585μm.<ref name="Burrows"/> Cells cylindrical or barrel-shaped.<ref name="Guiry">Guiry, M.D., John, D.M., Rindi, F. and McCarthy, T.K. 2007. ''New Survey of Clare Island Volume 6: The Terrestrial Algae.'' p.98 Royal Irish Academy {{ISBN|978-1-904890-31-7}}</ref> Both unattached (''C. linum'') and attached (''C. aerea'') forms exist. The unattached plants form masses of twisted filaments<ref name="Burrows"/> the attached filament grow as tufts from a definite base.<ref>Newton, L. 1931. ''A Handbook of the British Seaweeds.'' British Museum, London</ref>

==Habitat==
In [[Ireland]] found in fresh water.<ref name="Guiry"/> Both attached and unattached forms are to be found in marine waters.<ref name="Burrows"/>

==Distribution==
Both ''C. linum'' and ''C. aerea'' are found around the British Isles and around Europe into the Mediterranean and [[Mar Menor]]. In North America it is to be found along the Atlantic coast and in California.<ref name="Burrows"/>
